dedupe_keys.name: regional probabilistic liquefaction hazard mapping for the sacramento san joaquin delta

description: REGIONAL PROBABILISTIC LIQUEFACTION HAZARD MAPPING FOR THE SACRAMENTO – SAN JOAQUIN DELTA is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "simulation", published or maintained by Michael Greenfield, Greenfield Geotechnical LLC (greenfieldgeotechnical.com). Using an approximately 750 square kilometer pilot study area, this project seeks to address the variability of liquefiable soil deposits by developing 3D Gaussian process (GP) models of groundwater depth, geologic deposit classification, soil liquefaction susceptibility classification, and penetration resistance. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "simulation" project. Keywords: liquefaction susceptibility, uncertainty, gaussian process, soil variability, geostatistical model, geospatial statistics. Published 2022-03-04. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
